description: P1.1 domain models in orchestrator-core + mirrored TypeScript types, AND the workspace/dependency-arrangement + CI changes forced by introducing the first crates.io deps into the libraries. This feature is FIRST because it decides how the offline baseline changes: adding serde/uuid/chrono (and later sqlx/keyring/tokio) to library crates means those crates can no longer build offline, mirroring the Phase 0 tauri-app situation. Establish the members/exclude arrangement and CI steps so the whole thing still builds in CI (authoritative) and document what remains offline-verifiable. Independent of FEAT-002/003 conceptually but must land first since everything imports the models and depends on the new build arrangement.
steps: Read hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml and its extensive rationale comments about the tauri-app [workspace] exclude and the offline crates.io constraint. Read .github/workflows/ci.yml. Read architecture.md Sections 7.1 (data models), 4.2 (ProviderConfig), 6.1 (ManualRoute/PrivacyTag/RouteSource), 3.2/3.3 (crate layout/deps), 10.4 (schema_version).

Add workspace-level dependency versions under a [workspace.dependencies] table in hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml for the crates Phase 1 needs: serde (features=["derive"]), serde_json, uuid (features=["v4","serde"]), chrono (features=["serde"]), thiserror. (sqlx, keyring, tokio, async-trait are added by the crates that need them in FEAT-002; you may add their versions here too for consistency.) Use recent stable major versions matching what Phase 0 tauri-app already uses where applicable (serde 1, serde_json 1).

Implement the domain models in orchestrator-core. Replace the placeholder in crates/orchestrator-core/src/session.rs (or a new models.rs module re-exported from lib.rs) with the Section 7.1 types: Conversation { id: Uuid, title, created_at: DateTime<Utc>, updated_at, persona_id: Option<Uuid>, conversation_pref: Option<ManualRoute>, privacy_tags: Vec<PrivacyTag>, enabled_tool_servers: Vec<Uuid> }; Message { id, conversation_id, role: Role, content: MessageContent, created_at, route: Option<RouteMetadata>, usage: Option<TokenUsage>, status: MessageStatus }; enums Role (System|User|Assistant|Tool), MessageStatus (Pending|Streaming|Complete|Error); MessageContent (text / tool calls / tool results / attachments variants); RouteMetadata (provider_id, model, rationale, source) and RouteSource (Manual|ConversationPin|Automatic); TokenUsage (prompt/completion/total tokens); AgentPersona { id, name, system_prompt, default_route: Option<ManualRoute>, routing_hint: Option<RoutingHint>, allowed_tool_servers: Vec<Uuid>, parameters: ModelParameters }; ModelParameters (temperature, max_tokens, etc.); RoutingHint (e.g. PreferLocal|PreferQuality); PrivacyTag (LocalOnly|Confidential, extensible); ManualRoute (provider_id, model); McpServerConfig { id, name, transport: McpTransport, permission_mode: PermissionMode, enabled }; McpTransport (Stdio{command,args,env} | HttpSse{url,headers}); PermissionMode (Ask|Allow|Deny); ProviderConfig { id: String, kind: ProviderKind, base_url: Option<String>, api_key_ref: Option<SecretRef>, extra: serde_json::Value } and ProviderKind (OpenAI|Anthropic|Bedrock|Gemini|Azure|LmStudio|GenericOpenAI). All structs/enums derive Serialize+Deserialize (serde) and Debug+Clone; use serde rename_all="camelCase" attributes so the DTO JSON matches the TypeScript mirror. SecretRef is defined in the secrets crate (FEAT-002) - to avoid a premature dependency, define a lightweight SecretRef newtype (String handle) in orchestrator-core models OR add a secrets dependency; choose the approach that keeps dependency direction correct (orchestrator-core may depend on secrets per Section 3.3) and document the choice.

Keep orchestrator-core::placeholder()/smoke test working OR update the smoke test to reference the new real types. If the placeholder() fns in providers/mcp-client/routing/persistence/secrets are still referenced by orchestrator-core's smoke test and those crates are not yet gaining deps, leave them; adjust only what is needed so the crate compiles.

Mirror every serde DTO into TypeScript in hybrid-orchestrator/frontend/src/types/. Replace the placeholder export in src/types/index.ts with real interfaces/types (Conversation, Message, MessageContent, Role, MessageStatus, RouteMetadata, RouteSource, TokenUsage, AgentPersona, ModelParameters, RoutingHint, PrivacyTag, ManualRoute, McpServerConfig, McpTransport, PermissionMode, ProviderConfig, ProviderKind, SecretRef). Field names must be camelCase to match the serde rename_all attributes. Add a header comment noting these are hand-mirrored from the Rust DTOs in orchestrator-core and must be kept in sync.

Resolve the workspace/exclude + CI arrangement. Because orchestrator-core (and in FEAT-002 persistence/secrets) now depend on crates.io crates, `cargo build --workspace` will fail OFFLINE just like tauri-app did. Decide and implement: which crates stay in offline-buildable `members` (the still-dependency-free ones: providers, mcp-client, routing) vs which move to `exclude` (those with crates.io deps: orchestrator-core, persistence, secrets, and tauri-app). Update hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml members/exclude accordingly, PRESERVING and EXTENDING the existing rationale comments in the Phase 0 style (explain the offline-vs-CI tradeoff, the EXIT PATH when network is available, and that CI is the authoritative gate). Update .github/workflows/ci.yml so it still builds/tests/clippies EVERYTHING: the offline members via `--workspace`, PLUS each excluded crate explicitly via `--manifest-path` (mirror the existing tauri-app steps). Ensure clippy runs `-D warnings` on all of them. Keep the frontend lint/format/vitest steps. Note: if a cleaner arrangement exists (e.g. keep all six libs as members and rely on CI network to resolve deps, moving only the offline `cargo build --workspace` baseline expectation), you MAY choose it instead - but you MUST document the tradeoff and ensure the offline sandbox can still run SOME meaningful `cargo` command green, and CI covers the rest. Whatever you choose, the guiding invariant is: CI green on all three OSes is the real gate; document precisely what is offline-verifiable vs CI-only.
Author all new files with LF line endings (repo .gitattributes enforces this). Run `cargo fmt --all` over whatever remains offline-buildable.

Attempt offline verification of whatever is still offline-buildable (e.g. `cargo build -p providers -p mcp-client -p routing` or `cargo build --workspace` depending on the arrangement chosen) and record results. For crates that gained crates.io deps and thus cannot build offline, do NOT attempt network installs; record them as deferred-to-CI in the feature findings, and verify they at least parse (cargo will fail at dependency resolution, which is expected and distinct from a code error - note this distinction in findings).
acceptance_criteria: All Section 7.1 domain models + ProviderConfig (4.2) + ManualRoute/PrivacyTag/RouteSource (6.1) exist in orchestrator-core with serde derive and camelCase rename_all.
frontend/src/types/index.ts contains TypeScript mirrors of every DTO with matching camelCase field names.
hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml members/exclude arrangement is updated with extended Phase-0-style rationale comments explaining the offline-vs-CI tradeoff and exit path.
.github/workflows/ci.yml builds/tests/clippies every crate (offline members via --workspace plus each networked crate via --manifest-path) under -D warnings, and retains frontend steps.
Whatever is offline-buildable compiles green with `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; crates deferred to CI are clearly documented in findings.
New files use LF line endings.
verification: From hybrid-orchestrator/: run the offline-buildable cargo build/clippy subset chosen (e.g. `cargo build --workspace` if libs stay members, or `cargo build -p providers -p mcp-client -p routing`) and confirm green.
Run `cargo fmt --all --check` and confirm no diffs on offline-buildable crates.
Manually diff the Rust DTO field names against the TS types to confirm the camelCase mirror is exact.
Confirm .github/workflows/ci.yml enumerates a build+test+clippy step for every excluded networked crate (grep the workflow for each --manifest-path).
findings:
IMPLEMENTED
- Domain models: crates/orchestrator-core/src/models.rs implements all Section 7.1 types (Conversation, Message, Role, MessageStatus, MessageContent[Text/ToolCalls/ToolResults/Attachments] + ToolCall/ToolResult/Attachment, RouteMetadata, RouteSource, TokenUsage, AgentPersona, ModelParameters, RoutingHint, PrivacyTag[LocalOnly/Confidential/Custom], ManualRoute, McpServerConfig, McpTransport[Stdio/HttpSse], PermissionMode), plus ProviderConfig (4.2) and ProviderKind, plus a lightweight SecretRef newtype. All derive Serialize+Deserialize+Debug+Clone with serde rename_all="camelCase"; the two content/transport enums use internal tagging (tag="type"). Re-exported from lib.rs at the crate root.
- SecretRef choice: defined as a lightweight String-handle newtype in orchestrator-core rather than depending on the secrets crate. Rationale documented in models.rs: Section 3.3 allows orchestrator-core to depend on secrets, but making secrets own a serde-derived SecretRef would force serde into secrets NOW and pull it out of the offline-buildable member set. Deferred: FEAT-002 reconciles this with the canonical secrets::SecretRef (re-export in one direction). Dependency direction stays correct (orchestrator-core -> secrets, never the reverse).
- Smoke test preserved (still references providers/mcp-client/routing/persistence/secrets placeholder()), plus new unit tests in models.rs asserting camelCase serialization, tagged-union shape, and round-trip.
- TypeScript mirror: frontend/src/types/index.ts rewritten with hand-mirrored interfaces/unions for every DTO, camelCase fields matching the serde output, with a header noting no-codegen/keep-in-sync and the Uuid->string, DateTime->string, Option->|null, tagged-enum->discriminated-union, Custom(String)->{custom:string} conventions.
- Workspace arrangement (hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml): orchestrator-core MOVED from members to exclude (it now carries crates.io deps unreachable offline), joining tauri-app. Members kept offline-buildable: providers, mcp-client, routing, persistence, secrets. Added [workspace.dependencies] table (serde, serde_json, uuid, chrono, thiserror used now; tokio, async-trait, sqlx, keyring declared for FEAT-002 consistency). Extended the Phase-0-style rationale comments covering offline-vs-CI tradeoff, the transitive path-dep validation of orchestrator-core in CI, and the network-available EXIT PATH (move back to members, populate Cargo.lock, collapse the per-crate CI steps).
- orchestrator-core/Cargo.toml de-inherits workspace keys to concrete literals and uses concrete dep versions (mirrors the tauri-app precedent) because an excluded crate has no workspace root to inherit from when built via --manifest-path.
- CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml): added explicit build/test/clippy(-D warnings) steps for orchestrator-core via --manifest-path (mirroring tauri-app), added explicit fmt --check steps for both excluded crates (cargo fmt --all skips excluded crates), updated the header rationale, and left a NOTE for FEAT-002 to add persistence/secrets manifest-path steps when they gain deps. Frontend lint/format/vitest steps retained.
- Cargo.lock: orchestrator-core dropped out of the offline workspace lockfile (expected; it is no longer a member, same as tauri-app). Committed as part of the change.

OFFLINE-VERIFIED (green in sandbox)
- cargo build --workspace (members) -> OK.
- cargo test --workspace -> OK (member smoke tests pass; note orchestrator-core's tests now run via --manifest-path/CI, not --workspace).
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings -> OK.
- cargo fmt --all --check -> clean; cargo fmt --check on orchestrator-core and tauri-app manifests -> clean.
- All manifests parse: cargo verify-project for workspace, orchestrator-core, and tauri-app all {"success":"true"}.
- TypeScript: tsc --noEmit --strict --skipLibCheck on the types file -> clean (checked via a temp copy since the sandbox has no node_modules).
- All new/modified files confirmed LF.
- Manual field-name diff of Rust DTOs vs TS types confirmed exact camelCase match.

DEFERRED TO CI (authoritative gate; cannot run offline)
- cargo build/test/clippy for orchestrator-core: fails offline ONLY at crates.io dependency resolution (HTTP 403 downloading the serde index), which is a NETWORK failure, NOT a code/compile error - this is the same, expected situation tauri-app has been in since Phase 0. The manifest parses and the code is written to spec; CI (network) compiles, tests, and clippies it via --manifest-path on ubuntu/macOS/windows.
- Frontend vitest/lint/format:check run in CI (no node_modules offline; npm registry 403). The standalone tsc strict check above is the offline proxy for type-correctness.

NOTES FOR SUBSEQUENT FEATURES
- FEAT-002: when persistence gains sqlx and secrets gains keyring, move both from members to exclude and add matching --manifest-path build/test/clippy/fmt CI steps (the CI header already carries a reminder). Reconcile SecretRef then. Keyring on headless Linux CI has no Secret Service, so secrets tests must use an in-memory/mock SecretStore behind the trait.
- The workspace.dependencies table already declares tokio/async-trait/sqlx/keyring versions for reuse via `<dep> = { workspace = true }` (in member crates) or concrete literals (in excluded crates).
